presentation.label: DigiTide
presentation.summary: A two-channel pedal for the Digitone's inputs: a wet channel (reverb, delay or grab) and an always-listening micro-looper that feed each other.
presentation.overview: DigiTide, by irpina, is a two-channel pedal for the Digitone mk1's audio inputs: a wet channel (REVERB, DELAY or GRAB, with FREEZE) and an always-listening micro-looper (ENV, TAPE or STRETCH, with OVERDUB) that pass sound to each other as ROUTING says. A CLOCK lowers the sample rate of both, and the delay and grab times can follow the Digitone's tempo.
highlights: A wet channel: REVERB, DELAY or GRAB, each with FREEZE.
An always-listening micro-looper: ENV, TAPE or STRETCH, with OVERDUB.
ROUTING sends each channel into the other.
CLOCK lowers the sample rate of both.
usage: Hold a track key, pick DIGITIDE in the Mod Menu and press YES.
Play into the inputs and pick the wet channel's mode (REVERB, DELAY, GRAB) on page 1 (SYN1).
Hold T1 to freeze the wet channel into a pad.
Press NO to turn DigiTide off and get the synths back.

access.location: Mod Menu: hold a track key
steps: Use a build containing DigiTide for the Digitone mk1 on OS 1.43 or 1.44; fxkit comes with it.
Hold a track key: the Mod Menu opens. Pick DIGITIDE and press YES.
Play into the inputs; NO turns it off and gives the synths back.

controls.name: Mod Menu (hold a track key)
controls.doc: Open DigiTide: it takes the audio engine and its page shows. Its Mod Menu entry also brings the page back after MIDI.

controls.name: SYN1, SYN2, FLTR
controls.doc: Its three pages: page 1 and 2 (the wet channel's TIME and MODIFY, the looper's LENGTH and MODIFY, CLOCK, MIX), page 3 the toggles. Pushing a knob sets it back to its default.

controls.name: AMP
controls.doc: The mixer: the inputs' levels and pans, balance, volume and width.

controls.name: LFO
controls.doc: Two LFOs on the stock LFO page; DEST aims them at its controls or the mixer.

controls.name: RECORD
controls.doc: LOCK mode: hold a trig and turn a control to lock it on that step; FUNC + a trig clears the step.

controls.name: MIDI
controls.doc: The stock UI for the MIDI tracks while it keeps playing.

controls.name: NO
controls.doc: Turn it off: the synths and the Digitone's own effects come back.

controls.name: T1 (hold)
controls.doc: FREEZE the wet channel: the tail holds and nothing new comes in.

limitations: While it is the active effect it owns the audio engine: the synths are silent and the Digitone's own effects are off. NO gives them back; the sequencer keeps running.
Its MIDI CCs follow the Chase Bliss MOOD MKII's published CC chart, so a controller set up for that pedal works with it. It is not affiliated with Chase Bliss and uses none of its code.
A beta from its author; not yet run on a Digitone Keys.
Its buffers use 4 MB of the Digitone's bulk memory (0x47300000-0x47700000), apart from the other effect pedals'.
Needs fxkit (it comes with it) and core 4.1 or newer, so on OS 1.44 it does not build beside KitBank 0.2.0, which builds only on the older core.

load.display: Runs in the audio render while it is the active effect, nothing while it is off
load.conditions: From the source: its render handlers process the inputs only while it owns the audio (fxkit's core_audio owner); its other handlers run on the UI side. The author's CPU readings are from the emulator only. Not measured on a unit in Modwerk.

hardware.summary: The author tested DigiTide 0.2 on a Digitone mk1 (release v0.2, 18 October 2026; built before the effects' rename, which changed only names) and checked it in digikit's emulator on OS 1.43 and 1.44. It is still a beta. This module pins the released files.
limitations: The author's report names no OS release, date or duration: testedOn is the v0.2 release date, and 1.44 is the newest OS its files support.
Not run on a Digitone Keys.
Not tested in Modwerk on a unit.

tests.summary: The author's released 0.2 files, pinned unchanged, linked locally with core 5.4 and Modwerk's fxkit 0.1.0: alone, beside each of the other five effect pedals, all six together, and beside DigiHealth and DigiTables on OS 1.43; on OS 1.44 every pair but KitBank (core 2.x only). Emulator captures show where it appears; nothing ran on a unit in Modwerk.

Modwerk adds elekloader's SDK headers digitone-mk1/core3.h and digitone-mk1/fxkit.h from tag fxkit-v0.1 (irpina, GPL-2.0-or-later), which the source includes.
